newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia wheat crop to fall in 97/98 - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia wheat crop to fall in 97/98 - ABARE.

text.p: Australia's wheat production will fall to 16.984 million tonnes in 1997/98 (June 30) after the current year's big crop of 23.116 million, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday.

ABARE presented its Outlook conference with the prospect of declining Australian wheat production and exports in response to lower prices and as part of a medium-term shift in Australian grains production slightly away from traditional crops of wheat, barley, oats and sorghum toward oilseeds and pulses.

Australian exports of wheat and coarse grains were projected to be lower by 2001/02 because of reduced crop sizes and expanding demand from the domestic livestock feeding industry, Rhonda Treadwell, manager of ABARE's agricultural branch, said in papers prepared for the conference.
Figures with ABARE's presentation project Australian wheat production at 16.72 million tonnes in year 2001/02.

Offsetting an overall six percent increase in world wheat production in 2001/02, plantings in Australia, Argentina and Canada in 2001/02 were expected to be below 1996/97 levels as growers responded to lower real prices, Treadwell said.
The total area planted to grains in Australia was projected to decline over the medium-term as sheep numbers increased and grain prices eased, she said.
Figures with the ABARE presentation project the Australian area planted with wheat falling to 9.59 million hectares in 2001/02 from 11.00 million ha in 1996/97 and 10.00 million ha in 1997/98.
Australia's total winter crop production is projected to fall by 14.0 percent to 30.0 million tonnes in 2001/02 from 1996/97, with wheat projected to account for 55.0 percent of the total.
Winter oilseeds production is projected to increase by 74.0 percent to almost 1.1 million tonnes by year 2001/02, she said.
The proportion of Australian wheat exported is projected to decline over the medium-term as a result of lower production and increased consumption, mainly for feed wheat, she said.

This forms part of the background to an ABARE forecast of a 17.0 percent decline in the net value of Australian farm production (gross value of production less costs) to A$2.50 billion in 1997/98 after a forecast 29.0 percent fall to A$3.1 billion in 1996/97.
World grain prices were expected to be under pressure in 1997 because of increased production in 1996/97 and prospects of another large world harvest in 1997/98, Treadwell said.
The world indicator price for wheat in 1997/98 was forecast to average US$143.00 a tonne to $193.00 a tonne, with the most likely outcome around $170.00 a tonne, she said.
This would be down on forecast average world wheat prices of $180.00 a tonne in 1996/97, 14.0 percent below the 1995/96 average.
